items: **Revenue = metal volume x metal price + alumina volume x alumina price.** Metal volume is capped at roughly 4.7-4.75 lakh t until the 0.5 MTPA smelter commissions around December 2030 or early 2031 [MC] (CALL May 2026). So within the five-year explicit period, **all volume growth must come from the 5th Stream**, and all metal growth must come from price.

**The 5th Stream is the only volume lever.** It takes refinery capacity from 21 to 31 lakh TPA [F] (AR2026 p.27). At full ramp that is +73% on 14.46 lakh t of external alumina sales, or roughly +19% on group revenue at FY26 realisations [E]. Management's FY27 contribution guidance is only 2 lakh t [MC] (CALL May 2026).

**The alumina price is the offsetting variable.** FY26 realised $376; management guides $300-310 for FY27, a decline of about 19% [MC] (CALL May 2026). Roughly speaking, the guided price decline cancels most of the volume the new stream adds in FY27 [E].

**The metal price is the swing factor and it is unforecastable and unhedged.** FY26 average LME $2,771.68 against $2,526.00 in FY25; Q1 FY27 running at $3,500-3,600 on Middle East curtailment; management expects $3,000-3,100 for the full year [F] (AR2026 p.45); [MC] (CALL May 2026). A $100 per tonne move is worth roughly Rs 412 cr of revenue on 4.74 lakh t [E].

**Cost is a second-order driver.** A 10% shock to every purchased input costs about Rs 800-970 cr of EBITDA - roughly a $200 LME move [E]. Within cost, the controllable levers (caustic consumption, captive coal, grid power elimination, superannuation arbitrage) are largely exhausted, and the pay revision from 01.01.2027 reverses one of them [MC] (CALL Feb 2026; CALL May 2026).

**Depreciation steps up when CWIP capitalises.** Management expects substantially all of the Rs 6,395 cr CWIP capitalised in FY27 [MC] (CALL May 2026); on a Rs 5,500 cr refinery asset that is roughly Rs 220 cr of additional annual depreciation at a 25-year life [E].
**Other income reverses as the cash pile is spent.** Rs 665.83 cr in FY26, 8.6% of PBT, on a Rs 8,407.74 cr balance that the smelter programme is intended to consume [F] (AR2026 p.79, p.81) [AI].

subsections.title: What the forecast deliberately does not assume

blocks.text: **The single largest gap: capital expenditure.** The model's capex rule generates roughly Rs 1,620 cr in year 1 rising to about Rs 2,510 cr in year 5, a five-year total of approximately **Rs 10,170 cr** [E], derived from the model's own inputs. Management's disclosed programme is roughly **Rs 2,000 cr in FY27, Rs 4,000-5,000 cr in FY28 and Rs 8,000-10,000 cr in each of FY29 and FY30**, for a smelter-plus-power commitment of Rs 23,000-24,000 cr net of the NLCIL power joint venture [MC] (CALL May 2026). **The model therefore funds less than half of the capital expenditure the company has told the market it intends to spend over the same window, and the assets that spending buys produce nothing until roughly FY31 - outside the explicit forecast period but inside the terminal value.** We do not adjust the fair values for this; we flag it as the most important single limitation of the base case [AI].

items: **No LME or alumina price path.** Growth is a median of historical revenue growth rates, which blends volume and price indiscriminately [F] (NUMBERS).
**No smelter capacity addition.** Correctly so - nothing commissions before FY31 - but it means the capex above buys no revenue in the model either [AI].
**No pay-commission step-up.** The CPSE revision is effective 01.01.2027 at a guided 10-15% on the employee bill [MC] (CALL Feb 2026; CALL May 2026).
**No mine-lease renewal premium.** South Block expires 19.07.2029, inside the explicit period, with an unknown royalty premium [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).
**No working capital absorption.** Working capital days are set to zero, so a doubling of revenue absorbs no cash [F] (NUMBERS).

**No credit for the cash balance.** Equity value is enterprise value less borrowings; the Rs 8,407.74 cr of cash and bank is neither added to equity value nor netted from the enterprise value, and the interest it earns sits in other income, which is excluded from EBITDA [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.81). **Readers should understand the stated per-share figures as excluding that balance. We do not produce an adjusted figure** [AI].

**No contingent liabilities, no ORISED exposure, no mine-closure top-up.** Rs 2,179.22 cr of contingent liabilities, an unquantified twenty-one-year tax exposure and the C&AG's Rs 519.18 cr provision claim are all outside the model [F] (AR2026 p.307, p.190) [AI].
**No dividend policy change, no equity issuance, no divestment.**

**The most important observation about this scenario set is not in the table. It is that the bear case assumes a 40% EBITDA margin - a level the company has achieved in exactly two of the last ten years.** The ten-year operating margin record is 14, 15, 25, 6, 20, 32, 16, 21, 45 and 44 percent [F] (NUMBERS). A 40% margin would have been the **third best year in a decade**. The bull case's 46% has never been achieved on a full-year basis, though the trailing twelve months is 47% and the June 2026 quarter was 51% [F] (NUMBERS). **The entire bear-base-bull range therefore sits at or above the top of the company's own historical margin distribution.** There is no scenario in this set that describes what FY20 (6%), FY23 (16%) or FY24 (21%) actually looked like [AI].

items: **We do not attach probabilities, and we would distrust anyone who did on a commodity producer.** The distribution of outcomes here is the distribution of the LME and the alumina price over five years, which no analyst forecasts reliably and which management explicitly declines to forecast: "It's very difficult to predict" [MC] (CALL May 2026).

**What can be said qualitatively.** The base case requires the 44% margin to persist for five years. Two of the drivers that produced it are exhausted (caustic consumption at 96 kg/t from 121; grid power purchases already near zero) and one reverses on 01.01.2027 (the superannuation arbitrage, against a 10-15% pay revision). That makes 44% harder to hold than to reach [MC] (CALL Feb 2026; CALL May 2026) [AI].

**The bull case is a price case.** Its 14.3% starting growth is roughly double what management's own FY27 volume and price guidance implies, and its 46% margin requires the war-elevated LME to persist - which management describes as "a very escalated thing due to war situation" [MC] (CALL May 2026) [AI].

**The bear case is not bearish enough.** It contains no scenario in which the alumina surplus persists *and* the LME reverts toward the $2,500 area seen as recently as FY25, which together would take margin well below 40% on the historical relationship. **A reader who wants a genuine downside case should look at FY23 (16% margin, Rs 1,435 cr PAT) or FY20 (6%, Rs 136 cr) in the ten-year record rather than at the bear column** [F] (NUMBERS) [AI].

**The one asymmetry in the shareholder's favour** is that the balance sheet makes the downside survivable rather than existential: nil borrowings, Rs 8,408 cr of cash, IND AAA/Stable, a 36% payout that can be cut, and a capex programme that can be deferred [F] (AR2026 p.81-82, p.171) [AI].

The current price of Rs 352 sits inside the grid at six of the nine combinations and is bracketed by the base row at Rs 339.2 to Rs 388.5 [E].

The valuation question for NALCO is not resolvable by refining the discount rate; it is resolvable only by taking a view on whether a 44% EBITDA margin is a new normal or a cycle peak - and the DCF assumes the answer rather than testing it [AI].

TTM revenue of Rs 19,338 cr at a 47% operating margin is the best twelve months in the company's history, and the June 2026 quarter alone ran at 51% on a war-elevated LME [F] (NUMBERS); [MC] (CALL May 2026). A 9.6x P/E on peak-cycle earnings is not the same thing as a 9.6x P/E. Second, **the enterprise value does not net off cash**. Our valuation data state this explicitly: the source page does not split cash out of other assets, so the Rs 8,407.74 cr of cash and bank disclosed in the annual report is inside neither the EV nor the equity bridge [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.81). subsections.title: Interpreting the DCF and its assumptions

items: **The base case values the company at Rs 361.3 per share against a price of Rs 352 - a 2.6% gap** [F] (NUMBERS). On the model's own terms, the stock is approximately fairly valued.

**But 67.9% of that value is terminal** [E]. The explicit five years contribute Rs 21,362.5 cr of the Rs 66,511.3 cr enterprise value; the Gordon terminal value contributes Rs 45,148.8 cr [F] (NUMBERS). The model's answer is overwhelmingly a statement about perpetuity, not about the next five years.

**The 15% WACC is conservative for this balance sheet.** Nil net borrowings, Rs 8,408 cr of cash, IND AAA/Stable domestic ratings and an interest cover of 78.5x even after a litigation-settlement charge [F] (AR2026 p.171); [F] (NUMBERS). The 1.15 beta is doing the work, and for a commodity producer that is defensible - but the sensitivity grid shows that dropping WACC to 13.5% at the same terminal growth lifts value to Rs 431.3 [F] (NUMBERS) [AI].

**The 5.5% terminal growth is a price assumption in disguise.** With metal volume capped until roughly FY31 and the refinery capped after the 5th Stream ramps, perpetual 5.5% nominal growth means perpetual 5.5% price growth in a commodity whose price has round-tripped repeatedly inside the ten-year record [AI].

**The 44% terminal EBITDA margin is the boldest assumption in the file.** Held flat for five years and then into perpetuity, against a ten-year range of 6% to 45% [F] (NUMBERS). **If a reader disagrees with one input, this should be the one** [AI].

**The capex rule under-provides against the disclosed plan**, as set out in the forecast section: about Rs 10,170 cr modelled over five years against a Rs 23,000-24,000 cr disclosed programme [E]; [MC] (CALL May 2026).

blocks.text: **Net interpretation, without a target or a rating:** on trailing peak earnings the stock looks inexpensive at 9.6x earnings and 7.1x gross EV/EBITDA with a 3.26% yield; on the model's own base case it is within 3% of fair value; and the model's base case embeds a margin the company has hit twice in ten years, a capex figure less than half of what management has guided, and two thirds of its value in a terminal assumption. **All four statements are true at once, and the reconciliation between them is the analyst's actual job here** [AI].

sections.title: What the price requires: the reverse DCF

blocks.caption: Reverse DCF - from our valuation data only
rows: Constant five-year revenue CAGR that makes the DCF equal today's enterprise value
At the base 44% EBITDA margin, the same 15% WACC and the same 5.5% terminal growth [F] (NUMBERS)
The fading 8.4% to 10.0% path expressed as a single rate [F] (NUMBERS)

blocks.text: **The price requires 8.4% compound revenue growth for five years** - marginally less than the base case's 9.2% equivalent, above the three-year record of 7.8%, below the five-year record of 14.8%, and below the nine-year record of 10.0% [F] (NUMBERS). On growth alone, **the market is not asking for anything the company has not already delivered across a full cycle** [AI].

**The reverse DCF solves for growth while holding margin constant, and for this company that is the wrong variable.** An 8.4% revenue requirement looks modest until you read what sits underneath it. Metal volume is capped at roughly 4.7 lakh t until FY31, so metal revenue can only grow through the LME price [MC] (CALL May 2026). Alumina volume can grow substantially through the 5th Stream - from 14.46 lakh t toward a possible 25 lakh t - but management guides the alumina price down about 19% for FY27, to $300-310 from $376 [MC] (CALL May 2026). **So the 8.4% the price requires is, in practice, a requirement that the LME stays at or above its war-elevated level while the 5th Stream ramps into a falling alumina price.** And the reverse DCF holds the 44% EBITDA margin fixed throughout, which means it asks nothing at all of the variable that has actually determined this company's earnings for ten years [AI].

The arithmetic of the volume-versus-price trade, from the disclosures [E]: a full 5th Stream ramp adds roughly 10 lakh t of alumina, about +73% on FY26 external alumina volume, which at FY26 realisations would be roughly +19% on group revenue. A 19% decline in the alumina price applied to the enlarged volume would remove most of that. Management quantified the FY27 version of this trade itself: the alumina price move is worth "maybe around Rs.1,000 crores or Rs.1,200 crores" adverse, against which a metal price of $3,000-3,100 would deliver "$400 more" per tonne than FY26's $2,674 average realisation [MC] (CALL May 2026). **The company's own framing is that FY27 growth is a price bet, not a volume story** [AI].

One further point a reader should hold. **Revenue growth is not the binding constraint on this valuation; margin is.** The FY26 result is the proof: alumina volume rose 31% and metal volume 3%, revenue grew 6.3%, and EBITDA margin still fell from 45% to 44% [F] (AR2026 p.79); [F] (NUMBERS). Volume growth arrived and margin fell anyway. **A reverse DCF that fixes margin at 44% and asks only for 8.4% revenue growth is therefore an easier test than the business faces** [AI].

**The bull's best rebuttal, stated as strongly as the evidence permits.** The 44% margin is not a price artefact alone - it is what a fully integrated producer earns when it owns its bauxite, its alumina, its coal and its power, and it has been achieved in both FY25 and FY26 on very different alumina prices ($595 and $376). The FY26 margin held at 44% *despite* a 37% collapse in the alumina price, because volume, caustic efficiency, captive coal and superannuation absorbed it [F] (AR2026 p.79-80); [F] (NUMBERS). That is evidence of resilience, not of a peak. On top of that: the metal market is projected in deficit (-0.880 Mn MT in CY2026) while alumina is in surplus, and metal is 73% of revenue [F] (AR2026 p.45, p.77); India's aluminium consumption is growing 11.4% a year against 1.4% production growth [F] (AR2026 p.78); China is capped at 45 Mn TPA against 46 Mn TPA of need [F] (AR2026 p.77); NALCO carries Rs 8,408 cr of cash and no debt, and the required 8.4% growth is below what it has delivered over five and nine years [F] (AR2026 p.81); [F] (NUMBERS). **On that reading the price is asking for less than the company has historically produced, from a balance sheet that cannot be forced to sell.** The counter-counter-argument is one sentence: every element of that case except the balance sheet depends on the metal price staying where a war put it [AI].

sections.title: Final thesis

items: **The integration is genuine, structural and cannot be bought.** Captive bauxite under leases running to 2029 and 2032, captive alumina transferred to the smelter at cost, captive coal covering 55% of a 72 lakh MT requirement and rising, and 96-97% captive power at Rs 3.15 a unit. This is why a commodity producer earns a 44% operating margin and a 40% ROCE [F] (AR2026 p.46-47, p.80); [F] (NUMBERS).

**The balance sheet makes the downside survivable.** Nil borrowings, Rs 8,407.74 cr of cash and bank, IND AAA/Stable, and cumulative free cash flow of Rs 12,197 cr over five years - accumulated through a year in which the alumina price fell 37% [F] (AR2026 p.81, p.171); [F] (NUMBERS).

**A 48% alumina capacity addition is essentially paid for and entering production**, taking the refinery from 21 to 31 lakh TPA with about Rs 5,000 cr of the Rs 5,677.4 cr already spent [F] (AR2026 p.27, p.46); [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

**The metal market is in deficit while the alumina market is in surplus, and metal is 73% of revenue** - so the mix is in the right place for the cycle the company's own data describe [F] (AR2026 p.45, p.77).
**Cash is returned and has been returned in every profitable year of the record**: Rs 11.50 per share in FY26, 36.32% payout, 3.26% yield [F] (AR2026 p.45); [F] (NUMBERS).
**The price does not require heroics.** The reverse DCF implies 8.4% compound revenue growth for five years, below the five-year and nine-year historical records [F] (NUMBERS).

**These are cycle-peak earnings and the record shows how far they travel.** Operating margin has been 6%, 16%, 21%, 45% and 44% within the last seven years. The trailing twelve months is 47% and the June 2026 quarter 51%, on an LME that management itself calls war-escalated [F] (NUMBERS); [MC] (CALL May 2026).

**Volume cannot grow for five years.** Metal is capped at roughly 4.7 lakh t until the smelter commissions around December 2030. Indian demand growth of 11.4% a year cannot add a tonne to NALCO's metal output inside the forecast horizon [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (AR2026 p.78).

**The one volume lever is being added into a falling price.** The 5th Stream expands the alumina business by 48% while management guides alumina realisation down 19% to $300-310 [F] (AR2026 p.46); [MC] (CALL May 2026).

**A Rs 23,000-24,000 cr capital commitment is being taken at the top of the cycle, with no disclosed IRR**, peaking at Rs 8,000-10,000 cr a year in FY29-FY30 against FY26 free cash flow of Rs 4,413 cr, for assets that produce nothing before 2031 [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (NUMBERS).

**Governance is in documented statutory breach**, with fines in six of the last eight quarters, three independent directors against eight required, a qualified secretarial audit and an Audit Committee that could not be reconstituted [F] (AR2026 p.150-151, p.171, p.189; PPT Sep 2026).

**The state auditor says the accounts overstate profit**, management disputes it, the statutory auditors did not modify their opinion, and the question has been referred to a third party [F] (AR2026 p.190-192).

**The controlling shareholder's objectives are not the share price.** Directors are appointed by Ministry order, hold no shares, have no options, and Rs 1,035.98 cr of the FY26 dividend went to the Government of India [F] (AR2026 p.150, p.12, p.325).

**The optionality most investors associate with this name does not exist.** The defence and aerospace alloy JV has been cancelled on a negative IRR; lithium, rare earths and gallium are all pilot-stage after five to seven years [F] (AR2026 p.228, p.90); [MC] (CALL May 2026).

items: **The good five years.** The 5th Stream ramps to 10 lakh tonnes by FY28, the Indonesian alumina surplus is absorbed as Indonesian and Thai smelters commission, the alumina-to-LME ratio recovers from 12% toward the mid-teens, the metal deficit holds the LME above $3,000, Pottangi and the 48 lakh MT coal ramp arrive, and the smelter is ordered on schedule and funded entirely from internal accrual. Revenue compounds in the low teens, margin holds in the mid-forties, and the company enters FY31 with a 0.97 Mn TPA smelter and no debt [AI].

**The middle five years - the most likely single path on the evidence.** The 5th Stream ramps a year later than planned, alumina settles around $300-330, the LME normalises to $2,800-3,000 as Middle East smelters restart, revenue compounds at 7-9%, margin drifts toward the high thirties as the pay revision lands and depreciation steps up, capex climbs to Rs 8,000-10,000 cr and free cash flow turns negative in FY29-FY30, the dividend is trimmed but not cut, and the cash balance falls from Rs 8,400 cr toward Rs 2,000-3,000 cr without any borrowing [AI].

sections.title: Research view

subsections.title: Where the price sits, and what drives the gap

blocks.text: At Rs 352 the shares sit **2.6% below the base-case fair value of Rs 361.3, 30.2% above the bear case of Rs 270.3 and 21.3% below the bull case of Rs 447.6** [F] (NUMBERS); [E]. Within twelve months the market has paid Rs 199 and Rs 445 for the same company [F] (NUMBERS). **No buy, sell or hold rating and no price target is offered in this report.**

**What drives the gap is not growth. It is margin.** The reverse DCF says the price requires 8.4% compound revenue growth for five years - less than the nine-year record of 10.0% and well below the five-year record of 14.8% [F] (NUMBERS). That test is easy. The test it does not run is the one that matters: every scenario in the set, including the bear case, assumes an EBITDA margin at or above the top of the company's own ten-year distribution. A 40% margin - the bear assumption - would have been the third best year in a decade [F] (NUMBERS). **A reader who believes 44% is the new structural margin for an integrated, captive-power, captive-bauxite producer should regard the stock as fairly valued with optionality. A reader who believes 44% is what the top of an aluminium cycle looks like should regard the entire valuation range as anchored too high** [AI].

Three further things drive the gap between the model and reality, in the same direction. **First, the model does not fund the disclosed capital programme**: roughly Rs 10,170 cr of modelled five-year capex against a Rs 23,000-24,000 cr commitment that management has put on the record [E]; [MC] (CALL May 2026). **Second, 67.9% of the base-case enterprise value is terminal value** [E], so two thirds of the answer is an assumption about perpetuity in a commodity. **Third, the model's equity bridge deducts Rs 60 cr of borrowings and does not add the Rs 8,407.74 cr of cash and bank**, and the interest that cash earns is excluded from EBITDA - which cuts the other way and understates the stated fair values by an amount we deliberately do not compute [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.81) [AI].

items: **This is not a one-to-two-year holding.** The single largest capital decision in the company's history - Rs 23,000-24,000 cr for a 0.5 MTPA smelter and 1,080 MW of power - produces nothing before December 2030 or early 2031, and consumes the cash pile that currently supports the balance sheet along the way [MC] (CALL May 2026). Anyone underwriting the expansion is underwriting a five-to-seven-year horizon [AI].

**Inside that horizon, the earnings path is not smooth and is not controllable.** Quarterly PAT in the last twelve quarters has ranged from Rs 187 cr to Rs 2,003 cr [F] (NUMBERS). Volume is capped, price is unhedged, and management explicitly declines to forecast the LME [MC] (CALL May 2026).

**The dividend is the only component of return that is visible in advance**, at 3.26% on FY26's Rs 11.50 per share and a 36.32% payout - and its continuation through the FY29-FY30 capex peak is not guaranteed [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.45) [AI].

**The position size implied by the evidence is one that can tolerate a 25-40% drawdown without forcing a decision**, because that is what this equity has done inside single twelve-month windows and what FY20 and FY23 did to the earnings base [F] (NUMBERS) [AI].

blocks.text: **The one disclosure that would change this analysis most is the smallest to make: a project IRR and the LME assumption behind it for the 0.5 MTPA smelter.** Everything else about NALCO - the integration, the balance sheet, the cash, the cap on metal volume, the alumina surplus - is already visible in the documents. Whether a Rs 23,000-24,000 cr commitment taken at a 44% margin earns its cost of capital is not, and the company has not said [AI].

blocks.text: **This is initial coverage.** No prior report file exists for this dashboard, so there is no predecessor set of numbers, guidance items, risks or thesis statements to test the current quarter against. Everything in this report is a first observation rather than a revision, and the guidance tracker in the governance part is constructed from the three available transcripts (November 2025, February 2026 and April 2026) rather than from a previous coverage note. The earlier research notes held on this company [F] (BOARD) are dashboard analyst notes, not company disclosure, and we have treated them as a prior view to be tested rather than as evidence - their central caution, that the 44% operating margin and 39.6% ROCE are cycle-peak figures and that a reader anchoring on current ROCE is anchoring on the top of a commodity cycle, is corroborated by the ten-year margin record in our statements data and is carried forward into this report's conclusions [F] (NUMBERS).

For the avoidance of doubt about the reporting period: this report covers the quarter ended June 2026 (Q1 FY27), but **no Q1 FY27 earnings call transcript was available** and the September 2026 investor presentation carries a "Highlights of Q1 FY2026-27" section header with no quantitative content in the version available to us. Every Q1 FY27 figure in this report therefore comes from our statements data rather than from company commentary, and the most recent management discussion available anywhere in the evidence is the April 2026 call on Q4 FY26 [F] (PPT Sep 2026; NUMBERS). **The next quarter's report should be able to test this one's guidance table against actual Q1 and Q2 FY27 disclosures** [AI].

blocks.caption: Quality control review of this report
rows: Industry figures (global 75.3 Mn MT aluminium demand, India 6.122 Mn MT consumption, 4.5% and 6.2-7.8% CAGRs) are labelled as industry context throughout and are never added to or blended with company revenue. An explicit illustrative share calculation is provided and labelled [E], together with the statement that metal volume is capped until roughly FY31 so TAM growth cannot reach revenue through volume

There is no order book and none is claimed; alumina is sold on monthly spot tenders and metal on a three-day LME reset. Management's aspiration to sign long-term alumina contracts is labelled [MC] and separated from contracted volume. The A-to-F discipline is applied in the business part of this report

Every cost of production, price forecast, capex plan, volume target, JV loss and project timeline sourced from a call is labelled [MC] with the specific call. Where a management claim is corroborated by audited figures - the cost of production cross-check against segment results - the corroboration is shown and labelled [E]

Reported as improving on a total-revenue basis (no customer above 10% in FY26 against one at 12.41% in FY25) and as concentrated within the segment (four customers each above 10% of Chemicals, Rs 2,483.89 cr, none named)

Full CFO / CFI / CFF decomposition provided, including the point that Rs 2,851 cr of the investing outflow is a term-deposit movement rather than capital expenditure, and that Rs 361.93 cr of FY26 CFO was a working-capital release
Current share count and market capitalisation used

Our valuation data use 183.923 cr shares; the company reports 183.66 cr. The 0.14% difference is immaterial to conclusions but is disclosed rather than smoothed over. Market capitalisation of Rs 64,741 cr and price of Rs 352 are used throughout
A year-by-year margin driver table separates the two explicitly, and the net conclusion - that price is four to five times the size of everything management controls - is stated rather than implied
All eight thesis breakers carry a numeric threshold against a stated current value

No customer, contract, order book, capacity, market share, guidance or date has been invented. Where something is not disclosed - country-level exports, per-JV financials, project IRR, cost of production in the statements, director ages, peer multiples, the carrying value of the idle wind plants, sanctioned bank limits - the report says so
[F], [MC], [AI] and [E] applied at statement level with a source id after each label. Page numbers are given only for the annual report and taken from its page markers

A dedicated side-by-side table in the operations part covers twelve items, distinguishing those that reconcile exactly (EBITDA definition, PAT basis, net worth, borrowings versus lease liabilities) from those that do not (capex, bauxite output basis, share count, whistle-blower complaints, the C&AG provision dispute, lease expiry dates, input price guidance)

Every fair value, projection, multiple, sensitivity and implied growth rate is taken directly from our valuation data and cited as such. No new valuation figure is produced. Where the model's omissions are material - the capex gap, the excluded cash, the 67.9% terminal weight - they are quantified in rupees or percentages of the model's own outputs and explicitly not converted into an adjusted fair value

The reverse DCF's 8.4% implied growth is tested against the three-, five- and nine-year records and against the bull case's 14.3% starting growth; the report's central valuation argument is that the reverse DCF tests the wrong variable because it holds margin constant

The strongest bull argument is stated at full strength in the priced-in section as a counter-argument to our own conclusion, and the bull case's evidence is presented in the final thesis without qualification before the rebuttal
No marketing adjectives; no rating; no price target; no recommendation. Governance failings are stated with the company's own mitigating explanation attached

Three areas where evidence was thin and conclusions are correspondingly hedged: (1) no Q1 FY27 transcript exists and the September 2026 presentation's Q1 section is empty of numbers, so all Q1 FY27 analysis rests on our statements data alone; (2) no peer set is disclosed anywhere, so no relative valuation is attempted; (3) cost of production, the alumina cost-curve position and all joint-venture financials exist only as management statements or not at all, so the moat's depth is corroborated indirectly rather than evidenced directly

summary.one_line: NALCO is a genuinely integrated, effectively debt-free bauxite-to-metal producer earning cycle-peak margins it does not control, trading within 3% of the base-case DCF value while every scenario in that model - including the bear case - assumes an EBITDA margin at or above the top of its own ten-year distribution.
bull_points: Complete backward integration is structural and cannot be bought: 100% captive bauxite under leases to 2029 and 2032, alumina transferred to the smelter at cost, captive coal at 40 of ~72 lakh MT rising to 48, and 96-97% captive power at Rs 3.15 per unit - which is why a commodity producer earned a 44% operating margin and 40% ROCE in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.46-47, p.80); [F] (NUMBERS).

The balance sheet makes the downside survivable and the expansion self-funded: nil borrowings, Rs 8,407.74 cr of cash and bank (up 55% year on year), IND AAA/Stable and IND A1+ ratings reaffirmed 04.11.2025, and Rs 12,197 cr of cumulative five-year free cash flow accumulated through a year in which the alumina price fell 37% [F] (AR2026 p.81, p.171); [F] (NUMBERS).

A 48% alumina capacity addition is essentially paid for and entering production: the 5th Stream adds 1.0 MTPY to 2.1 MTPY at a projected Rs 5,677.4 cr, with roughly Rs 5,000 cr already spent, trial and testing commenced June 2026 and the Chairman stating production from October 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.27, p.46-47); [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

Mix is on the right side of the cycle the company's own data describe: the metal market is projected in 0.880 Mn MT deficit for CY2026 while alumina is in 1.599 Mn MT surplus, and metal is 73% of revenue; India's total aluminium consumption grew 11.4% to 6.122 Mn MT against domestic production growth of 1.4% [F] (AR2026 p.45, p.78).

Management under-promises on everything it controls and returns cash consistently: FY26 alumina sales of 14.46 lakh tonnes beat guidance of 12-13 lakh, employee cost came in at Rs 1,721.20 cr against guidance of ~Rs 1,900 cr, captive coal hit 40 lakh MT exactly, and the dividend was Rs 11.50 per share at a 36.32% payout and a 3.26% yield [F] (AR2026 p.43-45, p.80); [MC] (CALL Nov 2025); [F] (NUMBERS).
bear_points: These are cycle-peak earnings and the record shows how far they travel: operating margin has been 6%, 20%, 32%, 16%, 21%, 45% and 44% over the last seven years, the trailing twelve months is 47% and the June 2026 quarter 51% - on an LME that management itself calls 'a very escalated thing due to war situation' [F] (NUMBERS); [MC] (CALL May 2026).

Volume cannot grow for five years: metal is physically capped at roughly 4.7 lakh tonnes until the 0.5 MTPA smelter commissions around December 2030 or early 2031, so Indian demand growth of 11.4% a year cannot add a single tonne to NALCO's metal output inside the forecast horizon, and the one volume lever - the 5th Stream - is being added into a price management guides 19% lower at $300-310 from $376 [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (AR2026 p.78).

A Rs 23,000-24,000 cr capital commitment is being taken at the top of the cycle with no disclosed IRR, peaking at Rs 8,000-10,000 cr a year in FY29-FY30 against FY26 free cash flow of Rs 4,413 cr, for assets producing nothing before 2031; the comparable downstream JV (UADNL, 60,000 TPA defence and aerospace alloys) was abandoned because 'even the IRR with the capex investment was coming negative' [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (AR2026 p.228); [F] (NUMBERS).

Governance is in documented statutory breach: board composition was non-compliant with SEBI LODR 17(1)(a) and (b) throughout FY26 with three independent directors against the eight required, BSE and NSE levied fines in all four quarters (Rs 7,51,660, Rs 5,42,800, Rs 5,42,800, Rs 5,31,000 at each exchange), the secretarial audit was qualified, all three independent directors ceased on 31.03.2026 and the next appointment took effect only on 14.08.2026 - after which the Audit Committee still could not be reconstituted [F] (AR2026 p.150-151, p.171, p.189); [F] (PPT Sep 2026).

The state auditor says the accounts overstate profit and management disputes it: the C&AG's supplementary audit asserts provisions understated by Rs 519.18 cr for Utkal D&E mine closure, PP&E understated by Rs 474.73 cr and FY26 profit overstated by Rs 44.45 cr; management replies there is no short provisioning and has referred the question to the ICAI Expert Advisory Committee, while the statutory auditors issued an unmodified opinion. Not reconciled - and Rs 6,395 cr of capital work-in-progress, 24.1% of total assets, has meanwhile earned nothing, after a decade in which roughly Rs 12,032 cr of cumulative capex moved net fixed assets by only Rs 407 cr [F] (AR2026 p.190-193); [E] (NUMBERS).
watch_points: 5th Stream tonnage in Q2 FY27 against a guidance that was cut from 5-6 lakh tonnes to 3 lakh to 2 lakh across three consecutive calls, and whether the Chairman's stated October 2026 production start held [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; CALL Feb 2026; CALL May 2026); [F] (AR2026 p.27).
Operating margin after the Q1 FY27 print of 51%: any move below 44% questions the base case, and two consecutive quarters below 40% would fall through the bear-case assumption entirely [F] (NUMBERS).

Realised alumina price against the guided $300-310, and the alumina-to-LME ratio against FY26's 12.04% (from 21.42% in FY25) - the cleanest single indicator of whether the Indonesian surplus is cyclical or structural [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (AR2026 p.45).

Board approval, capital cost and - critically - any disclosed IRR for the 0.5 MTPA smelter and 1,080 MW captive power plant, guided for approval in August-October 2026 with the EGA technology agreement already signed on 07.09.2026 and ordering targeted for April-May 2027; and whether the remaining independent directors are appointed and the Audit Committee reconstituted before that commitment is made [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS); [F] (AR2026 p.189).

Capitalisation of the Rs 6,395 cr CWIP, which management expects to be substantially complete in FY27 (about Rs 5,500 cr relating to the 5th Stream) and which will step up depreciation and lower reported PAT without touching cash; alongside the first pay-revision provisioning ahead of the 01.01.2027 effective date [MC] (CALL May 2026; CALL Feb 2026).
guidance: FY27 alumina production and sales: 'around 25 lakh tons of alumina production and sales we are planning. That is around 2 lakhs more than the previous year' [MC] (CALL May 2026).

FY27 contribution from the 5th Stream: 'this year, optimistic planning we have done of 2 lakh tons... Two lakh is the minimum we are targeting. It can go to maybe 3 lakh or 3.5 lakhs also, depending on the commissioning process' - cut from the 3 lakh tonnes guided in January 2026 and the 5-6 lakh tonnes guided in November 2025 [MC] (CALL May 2026; CALL Feb 2026; CALL Nov 2025).

5th Stream commissioning: 'In June, we are starting the commissioning process, which may take two, three months to complete it'; 'maybe in the last quarter only, we will be able to have the production from there'. The annual report states phase-wise trial and testing commenced June 2026 and the Chairman states production from October 2026, with stabilisation in H2 FY27 and capacity rising from 21 to 31 lakh TPA [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (AR2026 p.27, p.47).
FY27 metal production: 'This year, we have planned around 4.73 lakh tons of metal production', against 4.71 lakh tonnes in FY26 and a rated capacity of 4.6 lakh [MC] (CALL May 2026).

FY27 domestic alumina sales: 'This year, again, we are targeting to further increase go to around 2.5 lakh tons to 3 lakhs tons', against 1.38 lakh tonnes in FY26 and 40,000 tonnes in FY25 [MC] (CALL May 2026).

FY27 alumina realisation: 'what we are expecting for this fiscal, this financial year, it will be somewhere around between $300 to $310 average alumina pricing', against $376 realised in FY26 and $595 in FY25; management adds a financial impact of 'maybe around Rs.1,000 crores or Rs.1,200 crores' [MC] (CALL May 2026).

FY27 LME aluminium: 'We are expecting that it should be somewhere around average... somewhere around 3,000 it will come down once the wars are over'; elsewhere '$3,000 to $3,100'. Q1 FY27 was running at $3,500-3,600 when the guidance was given [MC] (CALL May 2026).
Q1 FY27 profit: 'we are expecting that profit of more than Rs.2,000 crores plus first quarter. Because price is in our favor.' Actual Q1 FY27 PAT was Rs 2,003 cr [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (NUMBERS).

Aluminium cost of production: 'Average cost is around Rs.155. It is around Rs.156 for the whole year... we are booking at a highest rate of Rs.160. In any case, it will not go beyond Rs.160,000' per tonne; alumina cost 'varies from Rs.20,000 to Rs.22,000' per tonne [MC] (CALL May 2026).

FY27 capex: 'This year that is '26-'27, we are targeting a capex of around Rs.2,000 crores'; FY28 'somewhere in between Rs.4,000 crores to Rs.5,000 crores'; FY29-FY30 'That will go to maybe Rs.7,000 crores to Rs.8,000 crores' and elsewhere 'Rs.8,000 to Rs.10,000' at peak [MC] (CALL May 2026).

Total expansion programme: smelter 'Rs.17,000 crores to Rs.18,000 crores and our power plant is around Rs.12,000 crores. Since power plant, we are going for JV, only 50%... So it will come down to around Rs.23,000 crores, Rs.24,000 crores'; smelter commissioning 'by December 2030 or maybe early 2031' [MC] (CALL May 2026).
CWIP capitalisation: 'I think 100% will be capitalized this year because the majority is towards the fifth stream expansion. It is around Rs.5,500 crores' [MC] (CALL May 2026).

FY27 captive coal: 'overall coal requirement is around 7.2 million ton... This year, we are targeting 4.8 million ton', with the environmental clearance 'almost under process, and we are very much sure that in the next coming three, four months, we'll get it' [MC] (CALL May 2026).

FY27 input costs: caustic soda from a FY26 average of Rs 42,177 to about Rs 45,000 per tonne for the first six months; CP coke from Rs 44,000 to Rs 56,000; CT pitch from Rs 53,000 to Rs 57,000; aluminium chloride from Rs 1,21,000 to Rs 1,30,000; HFO from Rs 46,000 to Rs 70,000; management conceded 'cost of production will increase' [MC] (CALL May 2026).

Employee cost and pay revision: 'Pay commission impact will start from January '27... average increase will be 10% to 15%', with roughly 250 superannuations a year offsetting; FY27 incremental cost 'Rs.100 crores maybe additional cost' on a Rs 1,700 cr base [MC] (CALL May 2026; CALL Feb 2026).

Hedging and fund-raising: 'Hedging, we are not doing. It's directly linked to LME'; on funding, under the EPC-smelter-plus-50%-JV-power model 'we may not require any outsource support to finance our project', against Rs 5,000-6,000 cr around FY28-FY29 under the alternative [MC] (CALL May 2026; CALL Nov 2025).

Pottangi bauxite mine: MDO appointed 09.12.2025 for 25 years; 'The operationalization of the mines is planned in Q3 of FY 2026-27, with production expected to commence from Q4 of FY 2026-27'; approach road work 'Pending (Local agitation)'. This replaces the November 2025 guidance of 'by June we have to start the mines' [F] (AR2026 p.48); [F] (PPT Sep 2026); [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

New products: 'Around 60,000 tons of wire rod mill we are going in. It will take around two years'; rolled products 'on an average, we are doing around 2,000 per month. We are targeting from this year onwards around 2,500 tons per month'; no special grade alumina in the new capex [MC] (CALL May 2026).

Downstream JV reversed: the Utkarsha Aluminium Dhatu Nigam JV with MIDHANI for a 60,000 TPA high-end alloy plant is not proceeding - 'the requirement in the transportation sector has not grown like that... Even the IRR with the capex investment was coming negative'; the Board consented to winding up on 10.04.2026, with Ministry of Mines and DIPAM clearance pending [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (AR2026 p.228).

Other FY27 items disclosed with dates: alternate bauxite crushing and conveying from Panchpatmali South Block (Rs 496 cr, 93% complete at 31.05.2026) scheduled operational by October 2026; 15 MW of wind at Kayathar with four turbines in Q2 FY27 and six by Q3 FY27; Utkal-D&E capacity being raised from 40 to 48 lakh tonnes per annum with approvals pending; FY27 CSR obligation Rs 117.80 cr against Rs 79.13 cr in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.28, p.47); [F] (PPT Sep 2026).

No revenue, EBITDA, margin or order-book guidance is given in any available transcript. Management's only margin statement is directional: 'Overall margin will not go down. You see our overall revenues, around 70% of our revenues is coming from metal... So we are getting better margins on aluminium. So it will not reduce it. In fact, it will increase our margins' [MC] (CALL May 2026).
